KeysToEntries.Journal3Entry:
May my tongue blister for the things I said to you, my brothers. All because Conchobar swore he knew where our fortune had gone! I followed him over the Burning Spire and into Kalphite claws, while he pointed at wonders only he could see. Now Conchobar’s left me here to chase something broad and fluttering in the sky while I count my wounds.

I traded my good brothers for his promises, his lies. If our fortune is still out there, it can rot somewhere beyond those Kalphite-infested sands. I’ve had my fill of claws, scorched sand and promises of gold. Let whichever fool finds it next keep the lot.
KeysToEntries.Journal2Entry:
You have surely abandoned me, brothers, but I know the truth! Haha! The things I have seen! We accused the wrong thief! The Burning Spire may have roasted me, but from here I saw more than any of you. While you fools accused each other, I watched our fortune drift farther into the desert between you.

Keep walking! The desert will finish you as surely as it will finish me. Look at us, scattered across the desert with our fortune somewhere in the middle, and not one of you has the sense to see it! We shall arrive penniless at death’s door together, and I can’t wait to see the looks on your faces.
KeysToEntries.Journal1Entry:
No honour amongst thieves they say - not even my own brothers! We could’ve carried out double the take if Ferchar hadn’t insisted on bringing that ugly fabric with us. The chest would’ve been easier to carry with all four of us. Now, we’re left with nothing. Floated away with the desert sands? Likely story. I could’ve sworn that ugly rug was on the other side of the fire when we turned in, but one of them must have moved it. One of them must have buried our fortune in the night. Perhaps they’re all in on it. Rob the youngest of his share, as always!

Let the three of them chase each other across the Burning Spire if they wish. I’m staying right here, where we made camp. Whoever buried our prize must return eventually, and when they do, I'll be waiting. My waterskin may be empty, but my wits remain. Chase your own tails, brothers. I’ll have no part in it.
KeysToEntries.Journal4Entry:
Our fortune has taken to the sky! A floating treasure chest. Airborne doubloons! I have seen it! There it goes again, mocking me. I swear there’s something spread beneath it, corners flapping in the wind. Around the pyramid again, always just ahead of me. I can see it dancing over the stones.

One more turn and I’ll catch it. Then I’ll bring back every coin, embrace my brothers and divide it fairly. They’ll forgive me. They must. No one need hear what we said. Just one more turn...
KeysToEntries.Journal5Entry:
Those four fools thought they had stolen an ordinary carpet. Ha! Not once did they realise I could hear every word. I let them carry me from that dreadful vault, lay me beside their campfire and fall fast asleep. Then I slipped away with their chest and left them to blame one another. Such accusations! Such language!

Three of them chased me halfway across the desert before greed did the rest. I buried the chest while they scattered after me, somewhere none of them would think to look twice. A fine spot for my fortune, high on a mesa where I could watch those fools scour the desert below. The broken ridge lay beneath me, the sinking sands beyond it, with Kalphites crawling amongst the gypsum.

Let them chase shadows while I enjoy the sun for once. Just five minutes in this warmth. After decades beneath that pyramid, I think I’ve earned it. Then I’ll collect my fortune and be on my way.
Assuming I can get these tassels moving again...
KeysToEntries.QuestDescription: Locate the four brothers lost treasure
